title: A correction needs a full uncertainty budget
incomingEvidence: R1B admits only known stable shared-gain recovery; exact different-alpha PCM rivals survive. The skeptic requires uncertainty that does not silently omit reference/systematic error.
question: Can bounded positive envelope observations produce a rigorous slope interval, and how do stated reference/drift limits change the physical-alpha interval?

model.observation: positive envelope amplitudes with a supplied absolute error bound; extraction error not measured here
model.logBounds: log(a_observed-delta) to log(a_observed+delta), only if every lower endpoint > 0

systematicPremises.unknownBoundPolicy: withhold any physical-alpha interval if either bound missing; still report recorded-channel contrast interval

controls: no-error point envelopes include alpha4 to 1e-12
independent deterministic observation errors inside box with 128 fixed-seed realizations
construct exact extremal log-box choices following weight signs and reach interval endpoints
floor case set one observed target amplitude<=delta: withhold whole frozen-window log interval; do not silently delete sample
unknown systematic bound withholds physical interval
stated differential beta_r-beta_s=.8 outside .4 budget: narrow interval need not cover alpha; explicitly retain failure
falsifier: An in-bound realization escapes the calculated interval, extremal log box fails to attain endpoints, or missing nuisance bounds produce a physical interval.
claimCeiling: Deterministic conditional interval arithmetic for provided envelope errors and explicit nuisance bounds; not a confidence interval, measured noise guarantee, or calibrated physical estimate.
loopA: Execute interval arithmetic and supplied-error synthetic controls.
loopB: Independent exact-weight/interval derivation and counterexample tests; admit only conditional bounds.
